_note:
Slots for [brg_home-community]. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {token} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Slot names are underscore-only. Defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters — a literal `&` and a literal `—`, never `&` or `—`. THE

IS NOT WIRED, and this one is structural rather than awaiting anybody: it carries BOTH a hard
AND an inline marker block. No slot type can hold either — text/textarea escape them into visible markup, and html is an ACF wysiwyg that returns

-wrapped content. The field cannot express the design. Same call as careers-apply's heading. The two image plates and their counter-signed parallax are motion/photography and stay as code; the stand-in photography is tracked as `real-photography`. THE FIRST PARAGRAPH IS intro_1/intro_emphasis/intro_2, NOT body_0 — and the odd numbering is deliberate. It was missed in the first pass (2026-08-13) because the survey regex used to find text was `]*>[^<]*

`, which cannot match a paragraph containing inline tags — so the one wrapping was invisible to the tool and therefore to me. @expo caught it. Rather than renumber body_1/body_2, whose ACF fields are already generated and live, the new paragraph gets its own name: renaming a live field orphans whatever an editor has already typed into it. Cosmetically inconsistent, safe. Leaving it unslotted would have been the worse kind of half-editable: an editor rewrites the founding story in the two paragraphs below while THIS one — which carries the founding claim and the 2013 date — silently contradicts them.

intro_1.label: Intro — before the emphasis
intro_1.doc: Opening clause, up to the colon. The space before the bold phrase is in the markup, so no trailing space here.
intro_1.default: Blacktop Restaurant Group started with a simple belief:

intro_emphasis.label: Intro — bold phrase
intro_emphasis.doc: Rendered bold, mid-sentence. A clause, not a paragraph.
intro_emphasis.default: that a great meal is really just an excuse to connect.

intro_2.label: Intro — after the emphasis
intro_2.doc: The rest of the paragraph. Carries the founding year, so it needs editing if that is ever restated.
intro_2.default: Since 2013, we've been growing a family of restaurant brands rooted in genuine hospitality, craft food, and a deep love for the communities we call home.

body_1.label: Body copy — first paragraph
body_1.doc: Plain text; markup is escaped. Write `—` as a literal em dash.
body_1.default: We're not a corporation chasing locations — we're operators who eat at our own restaurants, know our guests by name, and measure success by how many times someone walks out the door smiling.

body_2.label: Body copy — second paragraph
body_2.doc: Carries the live location counts, so it needs editing whenever they change — which is the main reason it is a field. Write `&` and `—` as literal characters. CROSS-SECTION FACT — this number also appears in `our-restaurants-brands` -> Board & Brew second paragraph, and `community-stats` -> Stat 1 figure. Going ACF-editable REMOVED the check that used to catch a mismatch: it was three greppable strings in the repo, and it is now three database rows that nothing repo-side can compare. If you change one, change all three. (`doc` strings are per-field by construction, so this warning has to be repeated in each — there is nowhere on this project that can hold a cross-section fact.)
body_2.default: Today, BRG operates 12 Board & Brew locations across San Diego and Orange County, plus Odie's Pizza Co. in Oceanside — and we're just getting started.
